name: Lithuania
summary: Since 2017, possessing even a small amount of drugs without intent to sell is a criminal offence (Criminal Code art. 259(2)); people who seek treatment can be released from liability.

poisonControl.name: Apsinuodijimų kontrolės ir informacijos biuras (Poison Control and Information Bureau)

callingForHelp: No specific legal protection for people who call for help in a drug emergency was found.

euReach.title: Dáil answer on nitrous oxide incl. EU REACH consumer restriction (Sept 2026), HRB National Drugs Library

lsd.note: Possession of any amount is a criminal offence (small amounts: fine, community service or arrest).

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin mushrooms are controlled; possession is an offence and growing them is a crime.

dmt.note: DMT is controlled; ayahuasca is treated as a DMT preparation.

mescaline.note: Mescaline is controlled; possession is a criminal offence.

dox.note: Controlled; possession is a criminal offence.

nbomes.note: Controlled; possession is a criminal offence.

2c-x.note: Controlled; possession is a criminal offence.

2c-t-x.note: Controlled; possession is a criminal offence.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT is controlled; other 5-MeO tryptamines are likely controlled as new psychoactive substances.

cannabis.note: Criminalised in 2017, including small amounts; medical cannabis isn't available. Hemp products up to 0.3% THC are legal.

ketamine.note: Controlled medicine: possession without a prescription is a criminal offence.

mxe.note: Controlled; possession is a criminal offence.

dxm.note: Not verified. DXM is not under the UN drug conventions; whether it is OTC or prescription-only in Lithuania was not confirmed.

nitrous.note: Not a controlled drug; national sales rules not verified. EU ban on consumer sales expected from Feb 2027.

amphetamines.note: Possession of any amount is a criminal offence. ADHD medicines are legal with a prescription.

mdma.note: Possession of any amount is a criminal offence.

cocaine.note: Possession of any amount is a criminal offence.

caffeine.note: Legal, but selling energy drinks to under-18s has been banned since 2014.

alcohol.note: Legal from 20 (raised from 18 in 2018); shop sales limited to 10:00–20:00 (Sundays 10:00–15:00).

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is controlled; possession is a criminal offence. Status of GBL/1,4-BD not verified.

opioids.note: Heroin and other opioids: possession of any amount is a criminal offence; legal only with a prescription.

tramadol.note: Prescription-only medicine. Whether unprescribed possession is itself an offence was not verified.

benzodiazepines.note: Psychotropic substances: possession without a prescription is treated like other drug possession.

maois.note: Medical MAOIs are prescription-only; harmala/Syrian rue not known to be controlled. Ayahuasca contains DMT (controlled).
